This memorandum establishes the Critical Work Day (CWD) schedule and attendance guidelines for all Direct Reports and Immediate Supervisors/Managers from October 2026 through January 2027. The policy aims to maintain operational stability, ensure adequate staffing during peak business periods, support payroll processing, and minimize attendance-related disruptions.

II. DEFINITION OF CRITICAL WORK DAYS
Critical Work Days are designated operational dates when employees are expected to report for work according to their assigned schedules due to anticipated high volume, payroll processing requirements, holidays, or staffing considerations.

The following dates and circumstances shall be considered Critical Work Days:

Paydays: The 10th and 25th of every month, unless the salary is credited earlier.

Payday Buffer Days: The calendar day immediately before and immediately after each payday, regardless of whether the payday falls on a weekend or holiday.

Holiday Buffer Days: The calendar day immediately before and immediately after every declared regular holiday or special non-working holiday.

Individual Rest Day Buffer Days: The working day immediately preceding and the working day immediately following an employee's scheduled rest day, based on the employee's approved work schedule.

When multiple conditions overlap, the date remains a Critical Work Day.

Mandatory Attendance: Employees must report for work in accordance with their approved schedules on designated Critical Work Days, unless covered by an approved exception or other applicable company policy.

Unplanned Absences: Unplanned absences on Critical Work Days will be reviewed and may be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with company policy.

Tardiness and Late Logins: Employees are expected to log in on time and be ready to work at the start of their scheduled shifts. Unauthorized late logins may be subject to disciplinary action.

Planned Leaves: Leave requests covering or affecting Critical Work Days must be submitted in advance and require prior management approval. Approval remains subject to operational requirements and applicable leave policies.

Unauthorized Leaves: Absences or leaves taken without the required approval may be subject to disciplinary action, consistent with company policy and applicable law.

f. Any other exceptional circumstances not listed above must be cleared with program Director and Human Resources.

I. PURPOSE
This memorandum establishes the Critical Work Day (CWD) schedule and attendance guidelines for all Direct Reports and Immediate Supervisors/Managers from October 2026 through January 2027. The policy aims to maintain operational stability, ensure adequate staffing during peak business periods, support payroll processing, and minimize attendance-related disruptions.

II. DEFINITION OF CRITICAL WORK DAYS
Critical Work Days are designated operational dates when employees are expected to report for work according to their assigned schedules due to anticipated high volume, payroll processing requirements, holidays, or staffing considerations.

The following dates and circumstances shall be considered Critical Work Days:

Paydays: The 10th and 25th of every month, unless the salary is credited earlier.

Payday Buffer Days: The calendar day immediately before and immediately after each payday, regardless of whether the payday falls on a weekend or holiday.

Holiday Buffer Days: The calendar day immediately before and immediately after every declared regular holiday or special non-working holiday.

Individual Rest Day Buffer Days: The working day immediately preceding and the working day immediately following an employee's scheduled rest day, based on the employee's approved work schedule.

When multiple conditions overlap, the date remains a Critical Work Day.

All Direct Reports and Immediate Supervisors/Managers are expected to observe the following requirements on Critical Work Days:

Mandatory Attendance: Employees must report for work in accordance with their approved schedules on designated Critical Work Days, unless covered by an approved exception or other applicable company policy.

Unplanned Absences: Unplanned absences on Critical Work Days will be reviewed and may be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with company policy.

Tardiness and Late Logins: Employees are expected to log in on time and be ready to work at the start of their scheduled shifts. Unauthorized late logins may be subject to disciplinary action.

Planned Leaves: Leave requests covering or affecting Critical Work Days must be submitted in advance and require prior management approval. Approval remains subject to operational requirements and applicable leave policies.

Unauthorized Leaves: Absences or leaves taken without the required approval may be subject to disciplinary action, consistent with company policy and applicable law.

Exceptions: Emergencies and other valid circumstances will be evaluated in accordance with established company procedures.

a. Hospital emergency confinement of the employee or immediate family member provided that medical records or certificate is made available the following day the employee returns to work.

b. Death of an immediate family member of the employee as defined in the company handbook.

c. The employee was sent home prior to the critical workday and is able to present a valid medical certificate immediately upon return to work.

d. The employee becomes a victim of a robbery or serious crime provided that sufficient records are provided the following day upon return to work e.g. police report, barangay report, medico-legal report etc.

e. The employee is unable to report because of a natural disaster e.g. typhoon, landslides, earthquake etc.

f. Any other exceptional circumstances not listed above must be cleared with program Director and Human Resources.

Designation as a Critical Work Day does not automatically cancel legally mandated leave entitlements or other rights protected by applicable law.

AreaOfOpportunity:
Call Observation and Coaching Summary – 
Call ID: 92588279
Incident Summary
Merryll informed me that she had a call with a potential call-handling issue, so I reviewed the interaction to identify what happened and determine the necessary coaching opportunities.

At the beginning of the call, the agent was heard laughing while talking to someone beside her, followed by the cx saying “Hello?” three times before properly engaging. The following areas of opportunity were identified:
- Lack of empathy: The agent did not acknowledge the customer's possible inconvenience caused by the delayed response.
- Improper call holding: The agent needs to demonstrate proper call management to avoid unnecessary dead air while attending to the customer's needs.
- Delayed response: The agent did not hear the incoming call notification promptly, resulting in a delayed greeting.
Agent's Explanation
During the coaching discussion, the agent explained that her PC went into sleep mode while she was waiting for a show to become available. She moved the mouse to reactivate the PC but did not notice that the FX audio device had changed from Jabra to FX Fonudar. Before the call came in, she had not noticed the change in the audio settings, which caused her to miss the incoming call beep and respond late.
Coaching Provided
1. Demonstrating Genuine Empathy

The agent was coached to acknowledge the customer's experience and provide a sincere apology when a technical issue causes a delayed response. For example:

“I'm so sorry for the inconvenience. I was experiencing a headset issue on my end, which is why I wasn't able to hear you right away. Thank you for your patience.”

The agent was reminded to maintain professionalism and ensure that the customer feels acknowledged and valued throughout the interaction.

2. Proper Call Holding and Avoiding Dead Air

The agent was reminded to communicate with the customer whenever additional time is needed to search for information or verify details. Instead of leaving the customer in silence, she should use appropriate holding statements, such as:

“May I place you on a brief hold while I check that information for you? Thank you for your patience.”

If additional time is needed, she should provide periodic updates and thank the customer for waiting to ensure that the customer remains informed throughout the process.

3. Seeking Assistance When Necessary

The agent was advised that if she is unsure how to address a customer's concern or fulfill a request, she should seek assistance from the appropriate higher department or support team rather than guessing or providing potentially inaccurate information. This will help ensure that the customer receives accurate information and appropriate assistance.

4. Checking Audio Settings Before Calls

The agent was reminded to check her headset and FX audio settings whenever her PC wakes from sleep mode or when she notices any changes to her workstation. She must ensure that the correct audio device is selected and functioning properly before handling calls to avoid missed notifications, delayed greetings, and potential customer dissatisfaction.
BiggestRock: The biggest behavior impacting the agent's call-handling and QA performance is the lack of technical readiness and consistent execution of proper call-handling procedures. The unverified change in FX audio settings resulted in a delayed response to the customer, while the lack of immediate empathy and proper holding statements affected the overall customer experience and professionalism of the interaction.
RootCause: The agent's delayed response was caused by her failure to verify the FX audio settings after reactivating her PC from sleep mode. She was unaware that the audio device had changed from Jabra to FX Fonudar, which prevented her from hearing the incoming call notification promptly. Additionally, the interaction revealed an opportunity to improve her awareness of professional call-handling expectations, particularly demonstrating genuine empathy when a customer experiences a delay and using appropriate holding statements to prevent dead air. These behaviors indicate a need to strengthen her technical readiness, attentiveness, and consistent application of the required call flow.
SmartGoal: For the next interactions Merryll will consistently demonstrate proper call-handling procedures by responding promptly to incoming calls, maintaining professionalism, showing genuine empathy when addressing customer concerns, using appropriate holding statements to avoid dead air, and checking her headset and FX audio settings before handling calls. She is expected to apply the coaching provided in all applicable customer interactions and maintain compliance with QA standards, as measured through regular call monitoring and follow-up coaching sessions.

Although the customer had already expressed interest in purchasing the item, Trixie accessed it through the Intelligent Recommendation (IR) tab instead of retrieving it from the Recent tab, where it was already available.

The coaching session was conducted to address this concern, reinforce the importance of following established order-entry procedures, and ensure that all transactions are processed accurately and transparently. Trixie was reminded that correct procedure must be followed even when the customer's intended purchase is clear and the transaction is completed successfully.

However, Trixie retrieved the bracelet through the IR tab instead of the Recent tab, where the item was already available. She then presented the bracelet by reading its description before proceeding with the order.

This sequence raised a concern that the transaction might have been attributed as an IR-generated upsell even though the customer had already intended to purchase the bracelet.

The concern is not simply whether the sale was completed, but whether the appropriate process was followed and whether the transaction was attributed correctly. Gaming and transaction manipulation are treated as Zero Tolerance Policy concerns; therefore, adherence to established procedures is essential.

The available findings identify a process concern but do not, by themselves, conclusively establish intentional manipulation. Any final determination must follow the appropriate review and validation process.

Possible contributing factors may include a misunderstanding of the correct workflow, insufficient attention to the customer's original purchase intent, or a lapse in following the established IR guidelines. These are possibilities that require validation rather than confirmed explanations.

During coaching, Trixie was reminded to clarify the customer's intended purchase, select the correct retrieval method, and ensure that the transaction accurately reflects the customer's intent. She was also given the opportunity to explain her actions and acknowledge the importance of compliance.

Discussion Highlights
Well-being & Recurring Health Concerns:
Checked in on the agent's health following recurring absences attributed to headaches.
Advised her to seek a formal medical check-up to rule out serious conditions.

Addressed her pattern of unplanned absences and reviewed expectations for the upcoming holidays.

Team Lead / Coach:
Submit the formal non-recommendation evaluation with documentation of the requested probationary extension.
Monitor the agent's daily attendance and schedule adherence closely, particularly through the upcoming holiday period.
Follow up on whether she completes a medical consultation for her recurring headaches.
Agent (Antone):
Maintain zero unplanned absences and honor the holiday attendance commitment.
Proactively manage sleep and schedule habits to prevent further medical downtime.

Recognition1: one on one session October 22
AreaOfOpportunity:
1. Dispatch Operations & Call Volumes
Call Tracking: AM tracker call volumes reached 800 in previous weeks, and leadership has mandated a reduction. Tracking needs refinement to verify how many received calls are strictly AM versus general/SP dispatch.
Intake & Verification Compliance: A key driver behind elevated AHT is that dispatch agents are still performing intake duties. Agents must follow standard training: call and verify customer address details prior to final dispatch.
Accident & Escalation Flow: Agents frequently place calls on hold waiting for LDT/accident management approvals. During operational pushback, a $20 incentive is being offered to successfully close cases.
2. Performance Tracking & AHT Focus
Behavior Trends: Customer review trends (notably Samsung) have declined, with repeated negative behaviors highlighted from previous weeks.
AHT Outlier List: Leadership requested a formal list next week of agents with AHT of 900 seconds and above. These agents will be targeted for week-on-week handling time reduction.
Tenure vs. Performance: Wave 1 and Wave 2 agents are being scrutinized—since the account launched in August, tenured agents are expected to operate without basic workflow bottlenecks.
3. Schedule, Coverage & Site Optimization
Phone Adherence: Agents must maintain at least 30 minutes of green phone time consistently across the entire week, especially through Saturday shifts.
RSA Coverage: Phone support coverage for RSA needs review for the week.
Sitewide Account Optimization: A sitewide "floating account" optimization is slated for November (target/benchmark: 1T 15 pages). While this team’s direct exposure is limited, site leadership will monitor attendance and roster efficiency closely.
4. Regularization, Attendance & HR Compliance
Probationary Criteria:
Agents with Corrective Actions (CAs) will not be regularized.
Formal evaluations are submitted at the 3-month mark for high performers recommended for regularization.
For agents with behavioral or attendance issues arising by the 5th or 6th month, probation may be extended or employment ended based on severity. Attendance reliability is the primary deciding factor.
Medical Submissions: Six agents are currently flagged for attendance/medical certificates requiring doctor-mandated X-rays and follow-ups.

Transition Period Complete: Ample adjustment time was provided to batches from graduation through September; full operational standards are now in effect.

Strict Roster Adherence: Monthly client schedules are fixed in advance and require exact adherence to assigned shift timings.
Stabilization Period: Original shift schedules have been reinstated under a one-month observation period running through November to monitor consistency and stabilization.
Key Takeaways & Action Items
Immediate Goal: Reach the minimum 7.5 daily productive hours and eliminate hour shortfalls.
Focus Through November: Adhere strictly to the reinstated monthly schedule during the observation period to protect the client contract.

The Four-Step Sales Strategy

Build a conversation around the customer's selected item.

Introduce another item naturally based on the customer's interests.

The agent must consistently monitor their Starmatic schedule throughout the shift to ensure adherence to the assigned intervals and prevent unnecessary discrepancies in overall service time.
Additionally, the agent is required to send a snippet or screenshot of their weekly Starmatic schedule to the team group chat for visibility and monitoring. This will help ensure that the assigned schedule is properly communicated and that any discrepancies or concerns can be identified and addressed promptly.

TaskDesc: Metrics (KPIs), Time & Attendance, Compliance (ZTP), System Logging — Today, a 1-on-1 coaching session was conducted to officially welcome our new agent from Wave 5 into production and integrate them into the team. We opened the session by celebrating his successful completion of training and nesting, establishing a supportive environment while reassuring the agent that leadership, Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), and floor support are readily available to assist as they adjust to handling live contacts. We then completed a comprehensive review of the team's Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). We discussed the balance between quality and efficiency, diving into Average Handle Time (AHT), Number of Calls (NOC), Number of Calls Surveyed (NOC SUR), Net Promoter Score (NPS), Low Contact Resolution (LCR), First Contact Resolution (FCR), and overall Quality Assurance (QA) standards, emphasizing that resolving customer issues correctly on the first contact while adhering to quality guidelines is our top priority. We thoroughly covered operational hours, timekeeping, and daily logging expectations. The agent was informed of the billable target requirement of 7.5 billable hours per day, equating to 37.5 billable hours per week. To ensure a seamless start to each shift and prevent technical issues from impacting live servicing, the agent was fully instructed on arriving on-site 30 minutes early to log into GlobalProtect and verify all system accesses. We also set clear expectations around schedule adherence, specifically highlighting the required adherence to assigned lunch schedules and designated breaks, including the 3-minute bio break policy. For accurate time tracking and queue monitoring, we walked through clocking in on time via KASOCIOUS and using AGERO HUB for logging shift hours, break tracking, and recording call drivers per servicing interval. Furthermore, the attendance process was reinforced: the agent must post "Team In" and "Team Out" notifications in the team GChat room upon arrival and shift completion, and any unexpected absences must be communicated to the Team Leader at least 4 hours before the scheduled shift so that roster adjustments or overtime (OT) coverage can be arranged. Finally, we conducted a crucial alignment on compliance, Zero Tolerance Policies (ZTPs), documentation, and technical support. The agent was briefed on strict compliance mandates, emphasizing that processing payments is strictly prohibited, professional conduct must be maintained at all times without disrespect, and any form of call manipulation or call avoidance will result in immediate disciplinary action. We reinforced the necessity of thorough, accurate note-taking on every customer account to ensure seamless contact history. To safeguard the agent's performance metrics during system disruptions, we explained how to use the WFM/RTA Technical Tracker to log any technical or system glitches in real time, ensuring lost billable hours are accounted for with full operational visibility. The agent acknowledged all discussed points and expressed readiness to begin live floor production.
EmployeeCommitment: Commit to arriving on-site 30 minutes prior to scheduled shift to log in to GlobalProtect, ensuring all system tools are ready before live servicing begins. Commit to maintaining 7.5 billable hours daily (37.5 weekly), strictly following scheduled breaks, lunches, and the 3-minute bio break limit, while accurately recording clock-ins on KASOCIOUS and AGERO HUB along with my call drivers. Will actively post "Team In" and "Team Out" status on GChat daily, adhere strictly to all Zero Tolerance Policies regarding payment processing, professional conduct, and call avoidance, practice thorough note-taking, and notify Team Leader at least 4 hours in advance if an unexpected absence arises.
LeaderCommitment: Commit to providing full, continuous support on the production floor to ensure a smooth transition from Wave 5 into live operations. Will pair the agent with a designated floor buddy/SME during their initial week, conduct regular floor sweeps to address real-time questions, and ensure immediate assistance is available during live calls. Will conduct weekly 1-on-1 coaching sessions to track performance trends across KPIs, celebrate progress, and provide targeted guidance on quality and handle time. Additionally, Commit to actively assisting the agent with logging system downtime on the WFM/RTA tracker to safeguard their billable hours and performance metrics whenever technical issues occur.
FollowUpPlan: Will be checking with agents schedule adherence, servicing hours, system tracking and KPI metrics on the next coaching session.

Payment Processing: DO NOT process payments under any circumstances. Violations carry a strictly enforced zero-tolerance policy and lead to immediate termination. Rudeness & Disrespect: Practice zero disrespect. Treat callers the way you would like to be treated, and remember that customer frustration is directed at the situation, not at you personally. Status Manipulation: Do not put yourself on busy without active tasks, do not take your lunch break all in one swoop, and do not manually flip your status to offline. Call Handling & Operational Conduct: Avoid unassigning jobs or avoiding escalations. Keep hold times minimal; excessive holds are prohibited. Never disconnect/release calls intentionally, and always call back immediately if a call drops. Warm transfer all callers—cold transfers are strictly prohibited. Workstation Departure: Never leave your desk while a customer is on the line, while actively handling a job case, or during idle time. 2. ITS Intake (Job Details Notes) Location Details: Record the exact site address, gate codes, and on-site contact name and phone number. Issue Description: Log exact problem symptoms and mark the priority level (Standard vs. Emergency). Customer Instructions: Document specific requests (e.g., "Call [X] minutes before arrival") and key location notes. Important Details: Note high-priority customer status (e.g., customer accompanied by a child or disabled passenger). Equipment Needed: List required job tools/assets (e.g., flat bed, dolleys, specific tools, or required certifications). B. Dispatch & Solutions (Internal Notes) SP Communications: Record technician name, direct phone number, confirmed ETA, and status (Tech En Route or Scheduled). Actions Taken So Far: Document full call history with dates and timestamps, sent/received messages, and PO issuance. Next Steps: Clearly outline what needs to happen next, along with the designated follow-up time and assigned owner.

Rudeness & Disrespect: Practice zero disrespect. Treat callers the way you would like to be treated, and remember that customer frustration is directed at the situation, not at you personally. Status Manipulation: Do not put yourself on busy without active tasks, do not take your lunch break all in one swoop, and do not manually flip your status to offline. Call Handling & Operational Conduct: Avoid unassigning jobs or avoiding escalations. Keep hold times minimal; excessive holds are prohibited. Never disconnect/release calls intentionally, and always call back immediately if a call drops. Warm transfer all callers—cold transfers are strictly prohibited. Workstation Departure: Never leave your desk while a customer is on the line, while actively handling a job case, or during idle time. 2. Note-Taking & Documentation Standards Ensure all notes logged into the system are accurate, complete, and detailed. A. ITS Intake (Job Details Notes) Location Details: Record the exact site address, gate codes, and on-site contact name and phone number. Issue Description: Log exact problem symptoms and mark the priority level (Standard vs. Emergency). Customer Instructions: Document specific requests (e.g., "Call [X] minutes before arrival") and key location notes. Important Details: Note high-priority customer status (e.g., customer accompanied by a child or disabled passenger). Equipment Needed: List required job tools/assets (e.g., flat bed, dolleys, specific tools, or required certifications). B. Dispatch & Solutions (Internal Notes) SP Communications: Record technician name, direct phone number, confirmed ETA, and status (Tech En Route or Scheduled). Actions Taken So Far: Document full call history with dates and timestamps, sent/received messages, and PO issuance. Next Steps: Clearly outline what needs to happen next, along with the designated follow-up time and assigned owner.

Meeting Agenda: Roadside Assistance Team Enhancement & Best Practices

Meeting Goal
Empower agents with actionable call-handling strategies, review essential compliance guidelines, and align on key performance metrics to secure the 1,000 PHP per agent incentive for September.

Agenda Topics
1. Welcome & Team Recognition
Opening Remarks: Gratitude for everyone’s hard work, dedication, and daily contributions.
Metric Accomplishments: Recognize individual and team performance highlights across key parameters.
2. Core Mandates & Compliance Reminders
Zero Tolerance Policy (ZTP): Absolute commitment to customer safety—if a call gets disconnected for any reason, immediately call the customer back. Never leave a caller stranded.
Call Avoidance Warnings: Making unnecessary calls to delay receiving cases is strictly prohibited under ZTP.
Payment Processing: Strict prohibition against taking credit card information or processing payments over the phone. We are Roadside Assistance, not Accounting.
3. Mindset & Identity: The Roadside Hero
Who We Are: Moving beyond ordinary customer service—acting as roadside heroes who get customers to their destinations safely.
Empathy & Perspective: Putting ourselves in the customer’s shoes. Understanding that angry or frustrated behavior is a reaction to their situation, not to us personally.
Genuine Engagement: Acknowledging their stress, offering sincere support, and delivering reliable care.
4. Incentive Scheme & Program Transition
September Incentive: 1,000 PHP up for grabs per qualifying agent.
Eligibility Requirements: 95% overall KPI performance, minimum 95% attendance, and zero Corrective Actions (CA) or Incident Reports (IR) for September.
Current Standing: Two weeks remaining to drive performance upward.
Upcoming Transition: Handover of the RSA program to AM Romeo next month as leadership transitions to AMD.
5. KPI Deep-Dive & Tactical Execution Tips
AHT & NOC (Not On Call / After-Call Work):
Target: ≤ 60 seconds.
Strategy: On inbound calls, click Avail immediately once documentation is complete. When placing outbound calls to Service Providers (SPs), manually select Busy status to avoid accruing extra NOC time.
Documentation & Notes Standard:
Intake Notes: Always place essential details in Job Details for SP visibility.
Dispatch & Solutions Notes: Record internal details in Internal Notes to prevent client call-outs.
Efficiency Tip: Maintain pre-saved note templates. Use Notepad with F5 for instant date-and-time stamps before copying into the system.
Quality Assurance (QA):
Target: Monitored weekly per agent.
Strategy: Strictly adhere to standard Job Aids for Intake, the SATT tool for Solutions, and Dispatch tools.
Self-Unassign Rate (SUR):
Target: 0.01% to < 4.0% (Must not be 0% or manually inflated).
Best Practice: Avoid manual unassignment for Customer Info Updates or ETA updates after adding notes—the system auto-unassigns these cases once saved.
Resolution Metrics (FCR, LCR, FDR):
FCR (First Call Resolution - Intake): Target 90%+. Complete all required intake fields on the first pass to ensure seamless completion down the line.
FDR (First Dispatch Resolution - Dispatch): Target 94%+. Successfully establish SP dispatch without missing account details.
LCR (Last Call Resolution - Solutions): Target 70%+. Effectively resolve the customer’s situation on the spot.
NPS (Net Promoter Score):
Mechanism: Triggered upon case completion for Intake and Solutions calls.
Cross-KPI Impact: Complete, error-free intake fields protect both FCR and NPS. Incomplete intake data causes dispatch errors, directly harming the intake agent's NPS and FCR scores upon job completion.
Solutions Handling: Mindful execution during complex workflows, such as marking jobs unsuccessful and creating new tickets.
6. Q&A and Action Items
Open floor for agent questions.

Empower agents with actionable call-handling strategies, review essential compliance guidelines, and align on key performance metrics to secure the 1,000 PHP per agent incentive for September.

Agenda Topics
1. Welcome & Team Recognition
Opening Remarks: Gratitude for everyone’s hard work, dedication, and daily contributions.
Metric Accomplishments: Recognize individual and team performance highlights across key parameters.
2. Core Mandates & Compliance Reminders
Zero Tolerance Policy (ZTP): Absolute commitment to customer safety—if a call gets disconnected for any reason, immediately call the customer back. Never leave a caller stranded.
Call Avoidance Warnings: Making unnecessary calls to delay receiving cases is strictly prohibited under ZTP.
Payment Processing: Strict prohibition against taking credit card information or processing payments over the phone. We are Roadside Assistance, not Accounting.
3. Mindset & Identity: The Roadside Hero
Who We Are: Moving beyond ordinary customer service—acting as roadside heroes who get customers to their destinations safely.
Empathy & Perspective: Putting ourselves in the customer’s shoes. Understanding that angry or frustrated behavior is a reaction to their situation, not to us personally.
Genuine Engagement: Acknowledging their stress, offering sincere support, and delivering reliable care.
4. Incentive Scheme & Program Transition
September Incentive: 1,000 PHP up for grabs per qualifying agent.
Eligibility Requirements: 95% overall KPI performance, minimum 95% attendance, and zero Corrective Actions (CA) or Incident Reports (IR) for September.
Current Standing: Two weeks remaining to drive performance upward.
Upcoming Transition: Handover of the RSA program to AM Romeo next month as leadership transitions to AMD.
5. KPI Deep-Dive & Tactical Execution Tips
AHT & NOC (Not On Call / After-Call Work):
Target: ≤ 60 seconds.
Strategy: On inbound calls, click Avail immediately once documentation is complete. When placing outbound calls to Service Providers (SPs), manually select Busy status to avoid accruing extra NOC time.
Documentation & Notes Standard:
Intake Notes: Always place essential details in Job Details for SP visibility.
Dispatch & Solutions Notes: Record internal details in Internal Notes to prevent client call-outs.
Efficiency Tip: Maintain pre-saved note templates. Use Notepad with F5 for instant date-and-time stamps before copying into the system.
Quality Assurance (QA):
Target: Monitored weekly per agent.
Strategy: Strictly adhere to standard Job Aids for Intake, the SATT tool for Solutions, and Dispatch tools.
Self-Unassign Rate (SUR):
Target: 0.01% to < 4.0% (Must not be 0% or manually inflated).
Best Practice: Avoid manual unassignment for Customer Info Updates or ETA updates after adding notes—the system auto-unassigns these cases once saved.
Resolution Metrics (FCR, LCR, FDR):
FCR (First Call Resolution - Intake): Target 90%+. Complete all required intake fields on the first pass to ensure seamless completion down the line.
FDR (First Dispatch Resolution - Dispatch): Target 94%+. Successfully establish SP dispatch without missing account details.
LCR (Last Call Resolution - Solutions): Target 70%+. Effectively resolve the customer’s situation on the spot.
NPS (Net Promoter Score):
Mechanism: Triggered upon case completion for Intake and Solutions calls.
Cross-KPI Impact: Complete, error-free intake fields protect both FCR and NPS. Incomplete intake data causes dispatch errors, directly harming the intake agent's NPS and FCR scores upon job completion.
Solutions Handling: Mindful execution during complex workflows, such as marking jobs unsuccessful and creating new tickets.
6. Q&A and Action Items
Open floor for agent questions.

"The primary emphasis of this session centered on three critical performance metrics: SUR, NOC, and AHT.

Primary Root Causes (""Biggest Rocks"")
Customer Handling & Active Listening:

A primary challenge identified is consistent understanding and active listening during customer interactions. Missing key details early in the call leads to repeating information, extended hold times, increased line time (AHT), and misdirected dispatch details that later result in self-unassigning dispatches (SUR).

SATT Tool Utilization & Process Comprehension:

Another core focus area is the full, effective utilization of SATT alongside a deeper understanding of standard roadside assistance protocols. Misinterpreting procedural steps or underutilizing live tool capabilities causes delays in documentation, directly inflating post-call work time (NOC).

Tool Utilization & Optimization Strategy
To improve call flow, reduce unnecessary handle times, and keep SUR strictly under the 4% threshold, both agents must enhance their execution across key support tools:

SATT: Utilize actively during the call for real-time tracking and documentation. Mastering SATT avoids backlogged wrap-up time (NOC < 60s).

AVA: Rely on real-time automated workflows and script guidance to ensure compliance with roadside processes and eliminate guesswork.

Manual Dispatch Tool: Ensure full procedural understanding before creating dispatches manually; accurate inputs prevent late task unassignments (SUR < 4%).

Chat PF: Escalate complex edge cases early via Chat PF whenever a customer concern falls outside standard procedures, preventing AHT spikes."

"Summary: Resignation Alignment & Offboarding Terms

* **Meeting Date:** September 16, 2026
* **Participants:** Janille Jane Egos , Maria Lourdes (Management) and Balmeo (Employee)

---

**Operational Context & Performance Dialogue**

Management met with Balmeo to address an impending resignation and bring clarity to the underlying performance and attendance concerns. During the discussion, Management challenged shifting rationales regarding account difficulty, schedule challenges, and personal bandwidth. Janille reinforced organizational expectations, noting that high call volumes and night-shift rotations are baseline parameters of the operational account. It was emphasized that employment commitments must be approached with professional accountability rather than as trial runs.

Despite the operational friction, Management acknowledged Balmeo’s transparency in reporting to work to discuss the transition directly, rather than resorting to an unexcused absence (AWOL).

**Offboarding Strategy & Action Plan**

To maintain account stability and fulfill contractual obligations regarding liquidated damages, the conversation pivoted to establishing a clear rendering timeline:

* **Contractual Expectation:** Standard exit protocols require a 30-day rendering period.
* **Agreed Timeline:** Management agreed to a structured offboarding period, establishing a strict minimum of 15 days, with an operational end-date target set for **October 10, 2026**, to align with full work-week completion and payroll cutoffs (an interim milestone of **October 3** was noted).
* **Compliance Conditions:** The departure process is contingent upon Balmeo submitting a formal resignation letter prior to the next shift and maintaining 100% attendance compliance with zero unscheduled absences throughout the rendering period.

**Next Steps**

Balmeo accepted the terms, committed to submitting the formal documentation, and returned to the floor to complete the shift. Management will track attendance and shift compliance through the final target date of October 10."

AreaOfOpportunity: Active Listening, Compliance, and AHT
BiggestRock: High Average Handling Time (AHT) caused by excessive After-Call Work (ACW) and extended dead air/repetition during customer interactions.
RootCause: agent  hesitates to multi-task during live calls—waiting until after call disconnect to type call documentation and remaining silent while navigating system tools. This leads to customer updates being missed, repeated questions, and high ACW.
SmartGoal: Reduce average call handle time (AHT) from 820 seconds to 630 seconds by October 31, 2026, as measured by weekly contact center performance metrics, by applying live documentation practices and proactive call control on 100% of calls.
TaskName: Live Documentation & Proactive Call Control Implementation
TaskDesc:
Apply standardized call shorthand/templates during live customer dialogue to complete 90% of call documentation before call disconnect.
Perform mandatory customer safety/security verification checks within the first 60 seconds of every applicable interaction.
Use active listening transitions and signposting (e.g., "I'm pulling up your account now while I verify your address...") to minimize silent pauses to under 5 seconds per tool transition.
EmployeeCommitment: Will use the updated documentation shorthand template on all live calls and verbally state tool actions to avoid dead air.
LeaderCommitment: Will conduct two weekly side-by-side coaching sessions (15 minutes each) focusing on live typing techniques and offer real-time feedback on safety compliance auditing.
FollowUpPlan: Review 5 audited call recordings for ACW time compliance, evaluate live documentation completeness, and assess progress toward the 630-second AHT target.

"Janneth demonstrates strong care for drivers, but her primary challenge stems from over-sympathizing and getting overly invested in finding a resolution herself rather than staying within roadside assistance operational boundaries.

Impact on AHT & NOC: Spending excessive time emotionally reassuring the customer and manually attempting to resolve complex dispatches inflates line time (AHT) and leads to post-call administrative delays (NOC).

Impact on SUR: When manual dispatches stall or become overly complex, tasks end up being self-unassigned late in the process, driving up the SUR metric."
KPI: "Attendance	100% AHT (Average Handle Time)	300 - 450 seconds NOC (Not on Call/ACW)	< 60 seconds NPS (Net Promoter Score)	> 80% QA (Quality Assurance)	> 90% Tow %	< 59% FCR (First Call Resolution)	> 76% FDR (First Dispatch Resolution)	> 94% OON (Out of Network)	> 80% LCR (Last Call Resolution)>75% SUR (Self Unassign Rate)< 4%"

"Customer Handling & Active Listening:

A primary challenge identified is consistent understanding and active listening during customer interactions. Missing key details early in the call leads to repeating information, extended hold times, increased line time (AHT), and misdirected dispatch details that later result in self-unassigning dispatches (SUR).

SATT Tool Utilization & Process Comprehension:

Another core focus area is the full, effective utilization of SATT alongside a deeper understanding of standard roadside assistance protocols. Misinterpreting procedural steps or underutilizing live tool capabilities causes delays in documentation, directly inflating post-call work time (NOC)."

AreaOfOpportunity:
## Sync up Session Summary

### 1. Tracker & Performance Issues (Alexa)

* **Status:** Alexa missed logging data into Sir GN’s tracker over the last 9 days due to being swamped with other tasks.
* **Requirement:**
* She must send an **email explanation** detailing why logs were missed.
* She must log all future calls—if screen recordings are unavailable for second-by-second detail, high-level call details must still be recorded.
* Goal: Reach **50 total logs** to enable data analysis.


* **Next Steps:** Share the relevant **team playbook** with Alexa for guidance.

---

### 2. Operational Impact: Intake, Dispatch & Solutions

* **NPS Trigger:** NPS surveys automatically send **only when a job is completed**.

#### Process & Metrics Breakdown:

1. **Intake Agents:**
* **Role:** Must complete all critical fields on the initial intake call.
* **Impact:** Missing info forces a second call to the customer, causing dispatch delays and customer frustration.
* **Metric Penalty:** Directly lowers the Intake agent's **NPS** and **FCR (First Contact Resolution)**.


2. **Dispatch Agents:**
* **Role:** Efficiently assign service providers once complete intake is handed off.
* **Impact:** Operational failures (e.g., provider lacking equipment, provider no-show).
* **Metric Penalty:** Results in an **FDR (First Dispatch Resolution)** markdown for the Dispatch agent.

Incident Date: September 15, 2026

On September 15, 2026, several unanswered/disconnected calls were identified during a random call evaluation for Asherah Camiro. Review of the recorded interactions showed no audio captured from the agent’s end, with the available recordings primarily reflecting activity involving adjustments to the audio settings in Jabber.

The identified calls occurred between successfully handled calls, where the agent was able to communicate with customers normally. This raised a concern regarding the unanswered/disconnected interactions and whether the issue was caused by a headset, audio configuration, Jabber settings, or another technical concern.

The following calls were identified for review: 92140917, 92141016, 92141082, 92140281, 92139944, 92139727, 92140477, and 92140458, all dated September 15, 2026.

The incident requires documentation and review to determine the cause of the unanswered/disconnected calls and whether a technical issue affected the agent’s ability to establish or maintain the required audio connection during the affected interactions.

Investigation Findings:

Call ID 92139727 – 10:29: Screen activity was present. Asherah accessed the audio settings in Jabber. CCTV shows that she was initially away/asleep at her station, then got up and began speaking after receiving the call.
Call ID 92139944 – 10:46: No response and no screen activity. CCTV shows that Asherah was physically present at her station.
Call ID 92140281 – 11:08: Screen activity was present, and Asherah accessed the Jabber audio settings. The recording showed the message “No microphone found.” CCTV shows that she was initially asleep at her station and got up when the call came in, attempting to speak with the customer. This interaction may indicate a legitimate headset/audio device issue.
Call ID 92140458 – 11:27 and Call ID 92140477 – 11:28: No response and no screen activity. CCTV shows Asherah stepping away from her station at approximately 11:24 and returning at approximately 11:29.
Call ID 92140917 – 12:03: No response and no screen activity. CCTV shows that Asherah was at her station but was changing the edge tape of a paddle at the time.
Call ID 92141016 – 12:16: Screen activity was present, and Asherah accessed the Jabber audio settings. CCTV shows her at the station, talking while adjusting the microphone. This may also indicate a legitimate headset/audio issue.
Call ID 92141082 – 12:27: Screen activity was present, and Asherah again accessed the Jabber audio settings. CCTV shows her at the station, talking while adjusting the microphone. This may also indicate a legitimate headset/audio issue.

Based on the investigation, there are calls where the available evidence suggests a possible audio/headset issue, particularly those where Jabber displayed “No microphone found” and the agent was observed attempting to adjust the microphone while at her station. However, there were also unanswered calls where the agent was either away from her station or engaged in an activity unrelated to handling the call.
BiggestRock: Failure to consistently maintain call readiness and ensure the audio connection is properly established while in Ready status, resulting in unanswered/disconnected customer calls.
RootCause: The behavior may be related to inconsistent monitoring of the Jabber audio connection and headset settings, particularly when transitioning between calls. The agent may not be consistently verifying that the audio device is properly connected and functioning before remaining in Ready status.
SmartGoal: Effective immediately, the agent will verify the Jabber audio device and headset connection before and during each shift, remain attentive while in Ready status, and promptly report any audio or system issues to the appropriate support team. The agent will maintain zero avoidable unanswered calls and demonstrate consistent call readiness through the next coaching review.

The agent will verify headset and audio functionality at the start of the shift and after any identified connection issue, remain available while in Ready status, and immediately escalate recurring technical concerns for proper investigation.
EmployeeCommitment: Asherah is expected to acknowledge the coaching and corrective action, remain at her workstation and attentive while in Ready status, properly manage any audio/headset issues, and immediately report technical concerns through the appropriate process. She is also expected to demonstrate consistent compliance with call-handling and workstation expectations moving forward.

AreaOfOpportunity:
Corrective Action – COCD Group III, Quality Section 3.9
The identified behavior is being addressed under COCD Group III – Quality, Section 3.9, which covers:

“Commission of call avoidance or acts that are not in accordance with instructions or training received for the proper handling of calls connected or handled, including but not limited to improperly or abruptly releasing calls, cold transfers, jumping queue, putting a call on hold for a long time or without valid reason, refusal to attend to or answer calls, and other similar or analogous acts.”

The provision further identifies the following as an offense under Call Avoidance:

“(g) Any other type of system manipulation or incident that may be construed as call avoidance.”

The action of changing the audio setting during an active customer interaction, resulting in the agent being unable to hear the customer while the customer's audio remained present in the recording, is being documented under the above provision as a system manipulation incident that may be construed as call avoidance.

Lenra was provided an opportunity to explain the circumstances surrounding the incident. She acknowledged the concern, accepted responsibility for her decision, and recognized that changing the audio setting was not an appropriate method of addressing an audio or connectivity issue.
Prior to issuing this Corrective Action, I discussed the detailed description of the identified infraction with Lenra to ensure transparency and to provide her with an opportunity to understand the concern and provide her explanation regarding the incident.

Based on the review of the call and the circumstances surrounding the incident, it was identified that Lenra changed her audio setting during an active customer interaction after becoming concerned about her KPI performance and the possibility of being placed on PIP. Following the change in audio setting, she reported that she could no longer hear the customer from her end, while the customer's audio remained captured in the call recording.

During the coaching and discussion, Lenra acknowledged that she intentionally changed the audio setting during the interaction and recognized that this was not the appropriate procedure for addressing an audio concern. She further acknowledged that her concern regarding her KPI performance affected her judgment at the time of the incident.
BiggestRock: The biggest rock is maintaining proper judgment and adherence to call-handling procedures when experiencing KPI-related pressure or concerns. Lenra’s concern about her KPI performance and potential PIP status contributed to her decision to change the audio setting during an active customer interaction, which may be construed as system manipulation or call avoidance. The priority is to ensure that performance concerns do not influence her handling of customer calls or compliance with established procedures.
RootCause: The behavioral root cause identified was a lapse in judgment influenced by KPI-related anxiety and concern about performance results. Lenra acknowledged that her concern about the impact of another sale on her KPI contributed to her decision to change the audio setting during the call. Rather than following the established troubleshooting process or seeking assistance, she independently modified the audio setting, resulting in an interruption to her ability to hear the customer. Coaching focused on reinforcing appropriate decision-making, process adherence, and the proper escalation of technical concerns.
SmartGoal: Lenra will demonstrate 100% adherence to the required call-handling and troubleshooting procedures during monitored interactions, with no recurrence of system manipulation or call-handling behavior that may be construed as call avoidance.

Meeting Agenda: Roadside Assistance Team Enhancement & Best Practices
Meeting Goal
Empower agents with actionable call-handling strategies, review essential compliance guidelines, and align on key performance metrics to secure the 1,000 PHP per agent incentive for September.
Agenda Topics
1. Welcome & Team Recognition
Opening Remarks: Gratitude for everyone’s hard work, dedication, and daily contributions.
Metric Accomplishments: Recognizing individual and team performance highlights across key parameters.
2. Core Mandates & Compliance Reminders
Zero Tolerance Policy (ZTP): Absolute commitment to customer safety—if a call gets disconnected for any reason, immediately call the customer back. Never leave a caller stranded.
Call Avoidance Warnings: Making unnecessary calls to delay receiving cases is strictly prohibited under ZTP.
Payment Processing: Strict prohibition against taking credit card information or processing payments over the phone. We are Roadside Assistance, not Accounting.
3. Mindset & Identity: The Roadside Hero
Who We Are: Moving beyond ordinary customer service—acting as roadside heroes who get customers to their destinations safely.
Empathy & Perspective: Putting ourselves in the customer’s shoes. Understanding that angry or frustrated behavior is a reaction to their situation, not to us personally.
Genuine Engagement: Acknowledging their stress, offering sincere support, and delivering reliable care.
4. Incentive Scheme & Program Transition
September Incentive: 1,000 PHP up for grabs per qualifying agent.
Eligibility Requirements: 95% overall KPI performance, minimum 95% attendance, and zero Corrective Actions (CA) or Incident Reports (IR) for September.
Current Standing: Two weeks remaining to drive performance upward.
Upcoming Transition: Handover of the RSA program to AM Romeo next month as leadership transitions to AMD.
5. KPI Deep-Dive & Tactical Execution Tips
AHT & NOC (Not On Call / After-Call Work):
Target: ≤ 60 seconds.
Strategy: Practice touch-typing at home (ASDF / JKL;) and utilize "type-and-tell" during live calls.
System Status Management: On inbound calls, click Avail immediately once documentation is complete. When placing outbound calls to Service Providers (SPs), manually select Busy status to avoid accruing extra NOC time.
Documentation & Notes Standard:
Intake Notes: Always place essential details in Job Details for SP visibility.
Dispatch & Solutions Notes: Record internal details in Internal Notes to prevent client call-outs.
Efficiency Tip: Maintain pre-saved note templates. Use Notepad with F5 for instant date-and-time stamps before copying into the system.
Quality Assurance (QA):
Target: Monitored weekly per agent.
Strategy: Strictly adhere to standard Job Aids for Intake, the SATT tool for Solutions, and Dispatch tools.
Self-Unassign Rate (SUR):
Target: 0.01% to < 4.0% (Must not be 0% or manually inflated).
Best Practice: Avoid manual unassignment for Customer Info Updates or ETA updates after adding notes—the system auto-unassigns these cases once saved.
Resolution Metrics (FCR, LCR, FDR):
FCR (First Call Resolution - Intake): Target 90%+. Complete all required intake fields on the first pass to ensure seamless completion down the line.
FDR (First Dispatch Resolution - Dispatch): Target 94%+. Successfully establish SP dispatch without missing account details.
LCR (Last Call Resolution - Solutions): Target 70%+. Effectively resolve the customer’s situation on the spot.
NPS (Net Promoter Score):
Mechanism: Triggered upon case completion for Intake and Solutions calls.
Cross-KPI Impact: Complete, error-free intake fields protect both FCR and NPS. Incomplete intake data causes dispatch errors, directly harming the intake agent's NPS and FCR scores upon job completion.
Solutions Handling: Mindful execution during complex workflows, such as marking jobs unsuccessful and creating new tickets.
6. Q&A and Action Items
Open floor for agent questions.
Final encouragement and commitment to hitting the 95% target.

If the customer is engaged, responsive, and open to recommendations, Louie may continue probing and offer relevant complementary items. However, if the customer appears to be in a hurry, gives short responses, or clearly states that they do not want anything else, Louie should respect the customer’s decision without repeatedly pushing additional offers.

The goal is to balance sales opportunity with customer experience—maximize upselling opportunities when appropriate while ensuring that the customer never feels pressured.

AreaOfOpportunity:
UNEXPECTED SILENCE , EMPATHY and DOCUMENTATION

The customer called to inquire about a 10K white gold chain. At approximately 02:26, there was no response from the agent's line, causing the customer to ask, “Hello, are you there? Are you hanging up on me?” The agent's line became responsive again at approximately 03:11, but the agent repeatedly said “hello” without acknowledging the customer's concern or demonstrating empathy.

The agent was coached that when an unexpected silence or audio interruption occurs, the customer should be acknowledged, reassured, and provided with an apology. An appropriate response would be:

“I'm so sorry, ma'am, for the silence. I'm still here with you. We experienced an issue on our line, but I'll continue assisting you.”

The agent was also reminded to document the reason for the interruption or any technical issue, such as a headset or audio problem, in the appropriate notes to ensure there is a clear record of what occurred during the interaction.
BiggestRock:
Improve customer communication and empathy during unexpected call or audio interruptions.

The agent needs to consistently acknowledge the customer's concern, apologize for the interruption, provide reassurance, and properly document any technical issue that occurs during the interaction.
RootCause: The agent did not have an established response or process for handling unexpected silence or an audio interruption. Once the line became responsive, the agent focused on re-establishing communication by repeatedly saying “hello” but did not acknowledge the customer's concern, apologize, or provide reassurance. The agent also missed the opportunity to document the possible technical issue for proper tracking.
SmartGoal: Improve the handling of unexpected silence and audio interruptions by consistently acknowledging the customer, apologizing, providing reassurance, and documenting the incident.
TaskName: Improve Handling of Audio Interruptions and Customer Reassurance
TaskDesc: The agent will properly handle unexpected silence or audio issues by immediately acknowledging the customer's concern, apologizing for the interruption, reassuring the customer that assistance will continue, and documenting the incident in the appropriate notes. Moving forward, I will continue to monitor the agent's calls, provide real-time coaching and feedback, and conduct follow-up call reviews to ensure the agent consistently demonstrates empathy, maintains communication, and follows the proper documentation process when call interruptions occur.

Recognition1:
QA Coaching Session – Interaction #91748879 QA Score: 81%

The agent maintained the interaction with the customer and made an effort to assist with the requested item. However, there were opportunities to improve active listening, item verification, proper hold procedure, and customer acknowledgment. These behaviors are important to ensure accuracy and prevent missed sales opportunities.
AreaOfOpportunity:
#ACTIVE LISTENING AND ITEM VERIFICATION

The customer clearly provided the item number multiple times, but the agent did not accurately capture the exact item requested. The agent also did not apologize or acknowledge the repeated clarification provided by the customer.

When a customer provides an item number, especially one containing letters and numbers, the agent should practice active listening and read the information back to the customer for confirmation. For item numbers containing letters, the letters should be spelled back to ensure accuracy.

COACHING PROVIDED:
I coached the agent to slow down, actively listen, and avoid assuming or proceeding with an item number without confirming it. The agent should repeat the item number back to the customer and spell out the letters for accuracy.

Example:

"Just to make sure I have the correct item, I have W-P-D-1433. Is that correct?"

This confirmation allows the customer to validate the item before the agent proceeds.

#2 PROPER HOLD PROCEDURE

The agent did not follow the proper hold procedure while attempting to look for the requested item. When additional time is needed to research an item, the agent should properly inform the customer, request permission to place them on hold when applicable, and actively use the hold time to locate and verify the requested product.
COACHING PROVIDED: I coached the agent to ensure that every hold has a clear purpose and that the time is used productively to research the customer's request through the appropriate system resources. The agent should return to the customer with an update rather than leaving the customer waiting without clear communication.

#3 MISSED SALES OPPORTUNITY
Due to the failure to accurately capture and verify the customer's requested item, the customer's need was not properly addressed and the potential sale was lost.
COACH PROVIDED: I reinforced that active listening and accurate item verification are critical not only for customer satisfaction but also for protecting sales opportunities. When the customer clearly provides an item number, the agent must make every effort to capture it correctly, confirm the information, and proceed with confidence.
BiggestRock: Strengthening active listening and item verification to ensure customer requests are accurately captured and sales opportunities are not lost.
RootCause: The agent did not consistently demonstrate active listening when the customer provided the item number multiple times. The agent proceeded without accurately confirming the item and did not use the appropriate hold process to verify the information. This resulted in an unsuccessful interaction and a lost potential sale.
SmartGoal: Improve active listening and accuracy by consistently repeating and spelling back customer-provided item numbers before proceeding with the request.
TaskName: Improve Active Listening and Item Verification
TaskDesc: The agent will consistently practice active listening by carefully capturing customer-provided item numbers, spelling back letters, repeating the complete item number, and confirming accuracy before proceeding. When additional research is required, the agent will properly place the customer on hold and use the hold time to verify the requested item through the appropriate system resources.
EmployeeCommitment: I commit to practicing active listening on every customer interaction, especially when capturing item numbers. I will repeat the complete item number back to the customer and spell out the letters to ensure accuracy before proceeding. When I need additional time to research an item, I will follow the proper hold procedure and use the hold time productively. I will also acknowledge and apologize when the customer has to repeat information due to an error on my part.
LeaderCommitment:
During the coaching session, I reviewed Interaction #91748879 with the agent and discussed the opportunities related to active listening, item verification, proper hold procedure, and the impact of these behaviors on the sales opportunity. I coached the agent to always repeat and spell back letters in item numbers provided by the customer to confirm accuracy before proceeding. I also reinforced the importance of properly placing the customer on hold when additional research is needed and using the hold time productively.

I further coached the agent on acknowledging the customer when information needs to be repeated and providing an appropriate apology when the agent misses information that was already clearly provided. Recognition1:
QA Coaching Session – Interaction #91761085

QA Focus: Complete and Accurate Information / Inviting and Professional Communication



Good job in presenting an upsell opportunity during the interaction and making an effort to recommend an additional item to the customer. The agent demonstrated initiative in introducing a complementary product. Moving forward, the focus is on ensuring that all product information provided is accurate and that recommendations are communicated using the appropriate terminology and an inviting tone.
AreaOfOpportunity:
#1 – Complete and Accurate Information
00:20 – Incorrect Product Information

At the 00:20 mark, the agent stated that item WPD1433 has 0.20ctw blue and white diamonds. However, the product description indicates that the item has 0.12ctw.

Providing inaccurate product specifications may cause customer confusion and can negatively impact the customer's purchasing decision.

COACHING PROVIDED:
I coached the agent to always verify product descriptions and details before communicating them to the customer. The agent should utilize the available system resources and product information to ensure that the carat weight, product features, pricing, and other specifications provided are accurate and consistent with the system.
#2 – Proper Upsell Terminology
The agent stated that the upsell item would "match" the item the customer was purchasing. Since the items are sold separately and are not specifically identified in the product description as a guaranteed matching set, the agent should avoid using the word "match."

Using "match" may create an expectation that the two items are guaranteed to be identical or specifically designed to match.

COACHING PROVIDED:
I coached the agent to use "complements" instead of "matches" when recommending a separate item, unless the product description specifically confirms that the items are a matching set.

Recommended phrasing:
"This is a great item that complements the piece you're purchasing today."
This allows the agent to position the product as a relevant recommendation without creating an inaccurate expectation.

#3 – Inviting and Professional Communication
During the interaction, the agent's tone did not consistently sound engaged or interested in assisting the customer. Although the information was being communicated, the delivery lacked the inviting and enthusiastic tone expected when assisting customers.
COACHING PROVIDED:
I coached the agent to be more intentional with tone, energy, and delivery. The agent should sound genuinely interested in helping the customer and should use an inviting tone throughout the interaction, especially when presenting recommendations or assisting with the customer's needs.

The agent was reminded that the way information is delivered is just as important as the information itself. A warm and engaging tone can help create a more positive customer experience and make recommendations feel more natural.
BiggestRock: Improving product accuracy and customer engagement by verifying information before communicating it and consistently using an inviting, customer-focused tone.
RootCause: The agent demonstrated an opportunity to strengthen attention to product details and approved terminology when presenting recommendations. The agent also needs to improve vocal engagement and demonstrate greater enthusiasm and interest when assisting customers.
SmartGoal: Utilize product descriptions and available system resources before providing product details and consciously apply the coached terminology and tone during every customer interaction.

TaskDesc: The agent will verify all product specifications through the appropriate system resources before communicating information to customers. When making recommendations, the agent will use accurate terminology such as "complements" rather than "matches" unless the product description confirms that the items are specifically designed to match. The agent will also practice using an inviting, warm, and engaged tone throughout each customer interaction.

I will use the appropriate terminology when making recommendations and will use "complements" instead of "matches" unless the product description confirms that the items are a matching set. Key Discussion Points & Action Items

1. Operational Updates & Schedule

Shift Setup & Overtime: Please ensure you are logged in and ready 30 minutes prior to shift/dispatch.

Wave 2 Graduation: Scheduled for Thursday, July 30. The onsite event will include certificates of completion, food, and recognition.

2. Training Focus: Customer Profiling & Pacing

To improve Sense of Urgency, QA scores, and NPS, we discussed matching customer profiles and managing vocal pacing:

Hazard / Panic: Match their urgent pace. Never say "calm down"—instead, offer firm assurance (e.g., "The service provider is en route").

Frustrated / Delayed: Maintain a firm, calm, and confident tone. Avoid sounding hesitant or in doubt.

Anxious / Lost: Speak at a steady, measured pace. Reassure them clearly regarding ETAs and utilize Google AI / Maps to pinpoint locations efficiently.

4-Step Pacing Framework:

0–10s: Safety Check & Vocal Diagnostic

10–30s: Mirror Pace & Reassure (Genuine Empathy)

30–90s: Dispatch & Location Identification

Closing: Final Assurance, ETA Hand-off, & Payment Details



3. Monthly Incentive Program Breakdown

AHT (<450s): 20%

FCR (>76%): 20%

NPS (>80%): 40%

QA ( >90%): 20%

Payout Structure:

95% – 100% Overall KPI: ₱1,500

85% – 94% Overall KPI: ₱1,000

(Eligible for the top 50% of agents meeting attendance, active phone status, and policy/gatekeeper compliance).

Payout Date: Incentive crediting for July will occur on August 25, 2026.

If you have any questions or require clarification on any of the points above, please feel free to reach out.



Eligibility Criteria
To qualify for the monthly incentive, associates must meet all of the following conditions:

Active Status: Be an active associate for the entire qualifying month.
Full-Month Duties: Handle inbound calls/production for the full qualifying month.
KPI Threshold: Achieve a minimum overall KPI score of 85%. 
Attendance Requirement: Have no more than three (3) days of leave during the qualifying month, regardless of leave type.
Gatekeeper: Have no Corrective Action (CA) or Incident Report (IR) or Client Escalation issued during the qualifying month.
Policy Compliance: Comply with all company and client policies and operational standards.

Note: Newly hired associates, internal transfers into the Agero program mid-month, or associates who did not complete the full month of call-taking/production duties are ineligible for that month's incentive.

## Executive Overview

Management outlined key expectations regarding workplace conduct, shift arrival logistics, and compliance deadlines. The session detailed the performance-based incentive program, upcoming scheduling changes, and introduced the Ajiro Hub platform to streamline operational tracking, QA reporting, and technical support.

---

## Professional Conduct & Compliance Requirements

* **Workplace Conduct:** Emphasized the necessity of maintaining professional standards and communication at all times. Employees are expected to ignore unprofessional conduct or mockery from others and focus on active participation and results.
* **Shift Arrival & Account Transfer:** Mandated that agents arrive **30 to 60 minutes early** for every shift to facilitate the transfer of Adjur and Arise accounts to company-provided mobile devices.
* **Compliance Assessment:** Completion of the **July 2026 Compliance Assessment** form is required by the end of the day. Failure to complete the assessment will result in an Incident Report (IR) issued by the Compliance Department.
* **Post-Shift Case Corrections:** Mandatory case corrections must be performed after every shift to maintain data and record accuracy.

---

## Production Incentive Program & Performance Metrics

Management introduced a monthly monetary incentive program designed to reward top-performing agents based on structured scorecard targets.

### Qualification Criteria & Schedule

* **Eligibility:** Must rank within the **top 50%** of the agent population based on overall goal attainment.
* **Conditions:** Agents must maintain active status, have **no more than 3 days of leave per month**, and maintain **zero Incident Reports (IRs)**.
* **Payout Date:** Disbursed on the **25th of each month**.

### Scorecard Breakdown & Incentive Tiers

* **Weighted KPIs:**
* **Quality Assurance (QA):** 40% weight (Target: ≥ 90%)
* **Average Handling Time (AHT):** 20% weight (Target: ≤ 450 seconds)
* **First Call Resolution (FCR):** 20% weight (Target: > 76%)
* **Net Promoter Score (NPS):** 20% weight (Target: 80%)


* **Payout Tiers:**
* **Top Tier (95% or higher overall KPI):** 1,500 monthly payout


## Scheduling & Operational Updates

* **Staff Reshuffle:** An upcoming staff reshuffle is scheduled for the following month.
* **Rest Days:** Dispatch teams will typically receive Saturdays or Sundays as their scheduled days off. Schedules for Response Service Agents (RSA) remain pending finalized client data.

---

## Systems & Operations: Ajiro Hub Onboarding

Management introduced the **Ajiro Hub** platform (accessed via Employee ID and password) to centralize operations and replace manual spreadsheet tracking.

### Key Platform Functionality

* **Performance Dashboard:** Displays real-time personalized weekly metrics, including Handling Time, First Call Resolution, and Service Level Reporting.
* **Operational & Administrative Tools:** Enables agents to request shift swaps, upload Quality Assurance reports, track call drivers, and view customer voice feedback.
* **Employee Rewards Store:** Features a portal where agents can view earned incentive balances and redeem credits for rewards.
* **Technical Support Logging:** Replaces legacy escalation tools with a centralized system for reporting technical issues (e.g., Global Protect VPN errors), requiring a description and screenshot attachment for submission.

Management outlined key expectations regarding workplace conduct, shift arrival logistics, and compliance deadlines. The session detailed the performance-based incentive program, upcoming scheduling changes, and introduced the Ajiro Hub platform to streamline operational tracking, QA reporting, and technical support.

---

## Professional Conduct & Compliance Requirements

* **Workplace Conduct:** Emphasized the necessity of maintaining professional standards and communication at all times. Employees are expected to ignore unprofessional conduct or mockery from others and focus on active participation and results.
* **Shift Arrival & Account Transfer:** Mandated that agents arrive **30 to 60 minutes early** for every shift to facilitate the transfer of Adjur and Arise accounts to company-provided mobile devices.
* **Compliance Assessment:** Completion of the **July 2026 Compliance Assessment** form is required by the end of the day. Failure to complete the assessment will result in an Incident Report (IR) issued by the Compliance Department.
* **Post-Shift Case Corrections:** Mandatory case corrections must be performed after every shift to maintain data and record accuracy.

---

## Production Incentive Program & Performance Metrics

Management introduced a monthly monetary incentive program designed to reward top-performing agents based on structured scorecard targets.

### Qualification Criteria & Schedule

* **Eligibility:** Must rank within the **top 50%** of the agent population based on overall goal attainment.
* **Conditions:** Agents must maintain active status, have **no more than 3 days of leave per month**, and maintain **zero Incident Reports (IRs)**.
* **Payout Date:** Disbursed on the **25th of each month**.

### Scorecard Breakdown & Incentive Tiers

* **Weighted KPIs:**
* **Quality Assurance (QA):** 40% weight (Target: ≥ 90%)
* **Average Handling Time (AHT):** 20% weight (Target: ≤ 450 seconds)
* **First Call Resolution (FCR):** 20% weight (Target: > 76%)
* **Net Promoter Score (NPS):** 20% weight (Target: 80%)


* **Payout Tiers:**
* **Top Tier (95% or higher overall KPI):** 1,500 monthly payout


## Scheduling & Operational Updates

* **Staff Reshuffle:** An upcoming staff reshuffle is scheduled for the following month.
* **Rest Days:** Dispatch teams will typically receive Saturdays or Sundays as their scheduled days off. Schedules for Response Service Agents (RSA) remain pending finalized client data.

---

## Systems & Operations: Ajiro Hub Onboarding

Management introduced the **Ajiro Hub** platform (accessed via Employee ID and password) to centralize operations and replace manual spreadsheet tracking.

### Key Platform Functionality

* **Performance Dashboard:** Displays real-time personalized weekly metrics, including Handling Time, First Call Resolution, and Service Level Reporting.
* **Operational & Administrative Tools:** Enables agents to request shift swaps, upload Quality Assurance reports, track call drivers, and view customer voice feedback.
* **Employee Rewards Store:** Features a portal where agents can view earned incentive balances and redeem credits for rewards.
* **Technical Support Logging:** Replaces legacy escalation tools with a centralized system for reporting technical issues (e.g., Global Protect VPN errors), requiring a description and screenshot attachment for submission.

Key Discussion Points & Action Items

1. Operational Updates & Schedule

Shift Setup & Overtime: Please ensure you are logged in and ready 30 minutes prior to shift/dispatch.

Wave 2 Graduation: Scheduled for Thursday, July 30. The onsite event will include certificates of completion, food, and recognition.

2. Training Focus: Customer Profiling & Pacing

To improve Sense of Urgency, QA scores, and NPS, we discussed matching customer profiles and managing vocal pacing:

Hazard / Panic: Match their urgent pace. Never say "calm down"—instead, offer firm assurance (e.g., "The service provider is en route").

Frustrated / Delayed: Maintain a firm, calm, and confident tone. Avoid sounding hesitant or in doubt.

Anxious / Lost: Speak at a steady, measured pace. Reassure them clearly regarding ETAs and utilize Google AI / Maps to pinpoint locations efficiently.

4-Step Pacing Framework:

0–10s: Safety Check & Vocal Diagnostic

10–30s: Mirror Pace & Reassure (Genuine Empathy)

30–90s: Dispatch & Location Identification

Closing: Final Assurance, ETA Hand-off, & Payment Details



3. Monthly Incentive Program Breakdown

KPI Thresholds & Weights:

AHT (<450s): 20%

FCR (>76%): 20%

NPS (>80%): 40%

QA ( >90%): 20%

Payout Structure:

95% – 100% Overall KPI: ₱1,500

85% – 94% Overall KPI: ₱1,000

(Eligible for the top 50% of agents meeting attendance, active phone status, and policy/gatekeeper compliance).

Payout Date: Incentive crediting for July will occur on August 25, 2026.

If you have any questions or require clarification on any of the points above, please feel free to reach out.



Eligibility Criteria
To qualify for the monthly incentive, associates must meet all of the following conditions:

Active Status: Be an active associate for the entire qualifying month.
Full-Month Duties: Handle inbound calls/production for the full qualifying month.
KPI Threshold: Achieve a minimum overall KPI score of 85%. 
Attendance Requirement: Have no more than three (3) days of leave during the qualifying month, regardless of leave type.
Gatekeeper: Have no Corrective Action (CA) or Incident Report (IR) or Client Escalation issued during the qualifying month.
Policy Compliance: Comply with all company and client policies and operational standards.

Note: Newly hired associates, internal transfers into the Agero program mid-month, or associates who did not complete the full month of call-taking/production duties are ineligible for that month's incentive.

Maintain 100% compliance with the sales process and avoid behaviors that may be perceived as gaming or manipulation.
