Recognition1: Jona May properly verified the customer and followed the correct scripting throughout the interaction. She also correctly handled the cancellation request beyond the 30-minute cancellation window by following the appropriate cancellation process.
AreaOfOpportunity: The opportunity identified in this interaction is the proper utilization of the Return to Sender (RTS) process. Jona May submitted an RTS request without first verifying the shipment's current location and proximity to the delivery address. According to the SOP, agents should review the shipment status and determine how close the package is to its destination before initiating an RTS request. If the shipment is only a few hours away from the delivery address, it is generally too late to reroute the package, and the order should instead proceed through the standard return process. Taking a moment to validate these details helps ensure the correct process is followed and prevents unnecessary RTS requests.
BiggestRock: Process compliance, specifically validating shipment details before initiating an RTS request.
RootCause: This behavior appears to stem from moving too quickly through the process without fully reviewing all available shipment information. While the intent is to resolve the customer's concern promptly, skipping the verification step can lead to the incorrect process being applied.
SmartGoal: By the next QA audit cycle, Jona May will achieve 100% compliance with the RTS process by verifying the shipment carrier, shipment status, and distance to the delivery address before initiating an RTS request on all applicable interactions.
TaskDesc: Before submitting an RTS request, verify the shipment carrier, current shipment status, and the package's proximity to the delivery address to determine whether an RTS request is appropriate or if the order should proceed through the standard return process.
Frequency: Every applicable interaction involving cancellation requests beyond 30 minutes or shipment interception requests.
EmployeeCommitment: I will always check on the RTS SOP and will make sure to put a note for the distance and time so that I will get used to it and avoid any further mistakes
LeaderCommitment: I will review RTS-related interactions during upcoming QA audits, provide timely feedback on process adherence, and reinforce the importance of validating shipment details before initiating an RTS request.
FollowUpPlan: Review future RTS interactions to confirm that shipment status, carrier, and delivery distance are consistently verified before action is taken. Reinforce correct decision-making and provide additional coaching if process gaps are identified.

Category: Attendance – Tardiness
COCD Reference: Group 1 – Provisions on Attendance, Section 1.18 – Incurrence of Tardiness, i.e., inability to be at the assigned workstation at the expected time.

Furthermore, I emphasized that punctuality is a key attendance expectation and that repeated incidents of tardiness may result in progressive disciplinary action in accordance with the Company's Code of Conduct and Discipline (COCD).
BiggestRock: Consistently report to the assigned workstation on or before the scheduled shift start time by practicing proper time management and advance planning.
RootCause: Needs to improve planning and time management for personal commitments to prevent conflicts with work schedules.
SmartGoal: Starting immediately, Ryson will report to work at least 10-15  minutes before the start of every scheduled shift and maintain zero instances of tardiness for the next 30 days. TaskDesc:
-Arrive at the workplace early enough to be logged in and ready before the scheduled shift.
-Plan personal activities in advance to avoid conflicts with work schedules.
-Submit RD or leave requests ahead of time for planned events.
-Notify the immediate superior at least four (4) hours before the shift if an emergency or unavoidable delay may affect attendance.
-Strictly comply with the attendance provisions outlined in COCD Group 1, Section 1.18.

conduct follow-up coaching if additional attendance concerns arise,

* Reinforced **Phone Readiness and Adherence** expectations, including:

Here's a consolidated **Huddle Discussion Points** version with all redundant items removed while keeping all key messages intact.

# Post-Shift Huddle Discussion Points

* Congratulated all Wave 2 agents for their hard work, dedication, and continued contributions to the team's success.

* Reinforced awareness of the company's **Zero Tolerance Policy (ZTP)**, particularly offenses involving call avoidance, unauthorized payment acceptance, and attendance-related violations. Agents were reminded that these are serious offenses and may result in immediate termination of employment.

* Reviewed the **Critical Working Days and Attendance Compliance Memorandum**, emphasizing that attendance is mandatory during designated critical working days, including periods before, during, and after paydays, holidays, and scheduled rest days. Agents were reminded to report to work on time, complete their scheduled shifts, promptly communicate attendance concerns, and comply with the Company's Code of Conduct and Discipline (COCD).

* Reminded all agents to check their **Starmatic schedules** before the end of each shift to stay informed of any schedule updates or changes.

* Reinforced **Phone Readiness and Adherence** expectations, including:

  * Logging in on time at the start of the shift.
  * Returning promptly from breaks and lunch.
  * Updating status immediately after offline activities.
  * Escalating technical or system issues immediately to minimize adherence impact.

* Reviewed current **NPS performance**, recognizing strong-performing agents while identifying opportunities for improvement among Watch, High-Risk, and Critical segments. Reinforced customer experience expectations by emphasizing empathy, professionalism, positive communication, proper opening and closing statements, urgency, accurate verification, and complete call ownership.

* Reinforced focus on achieving key operational metrics, including **QA, NPS, AHT, FCR, TOW, and SUR**, while consistently following company policies and standard operating procedures.

* Reinforced documentation and reporting compliance by reminding agents to:

  * Update the Agent Timing Report, Call Drivers, and Call Issue Tracker accurately and in real time.
  * Record all required information in the Details tab.
  * Include exact documentation timestamps, even when only Internal Notes are entered.
  * Ensure complete and accurate Swoop documentation before ending every customer interaction.

* Discussed the **July 4 Holiday Readiness – REACT: Leave No Customer Stranded** communication. Agents were reminded to:

  * Verify customer safety at the beginning of every call.
  * Offer to contact 911 whenever appropriate.
  * Demonstrate empathy, urgency, and full ownership of each case.
  * Follow the required Intake, Dispatch, and Solutions call flows.
  * Send the location link promptly.
  * Utilize all available resources, including AVA, the Knowledge Center, RS-SATT Solutions Tool, Manual Dispatch Tool, and Chat Support to efficiently resolve customer concerns.
  * Ensure no customer is left stranded, particularly during the high-volume holiday travel period.

* Cascaded the **HRIS Acknowledgement for the Mutual Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure Agreement** and reminded all agents to complete the required acknowledgement.

* Advised agents to carefully review their payroll during the payroll scrubbing period and immediately report any discrepancies or concerns to their Team Leader or the appropriate support team before the payroll cutoff.

Recognition1:
Call ID: 91331437
Date of the Call: JULY 6,2026

Call Observation

The agent proactively approached Team Leader Gerald to request a review of the call, as she was uncertain whether her actions could be considered gaming or manipulation. Team Leader Gerald immediately informed me about the call. Since its not my scheduled time shift yet  at that time, As her TL, I listened to the call as soon as possible to conduct a thorough assessment.

During the interaction, the customer called to inquire about item LGA496 and eventually decided to proceed with the purchase. The agent correctly read the product description and added the requested item to the customer's cart. Afterward, the agent asked the customer which color she preferred. While this confirmation is not necessarily required because the customer had already identified the item and was familiar with its description, asking for color confirmation is not considered an issue.

However, the concern arose when the agent added another item to the cart. Instead of selecting the opposite or matching variation intended for comparison, the agent mistakenly added the same item with a different total carat weight (CTW). The customer originally selected the item with a specific CTW, but the second item added was the 3 CTW version. The agent failed to carefully read and verify the product description before adding the item, resulting in an incorrect comparison.

After adding the second item, the agent navigated to the recommendation page and offered item LGA497, informing the customer that it was a lower-priced option than the item she was purchasing. Because the recommendation was based on the incorrectly added item rather than the customer's original selection, the recommendation process unintentionally influenced the customer's purchasing decision using an inaccurate comparison. This scenario falls under manipulation, as the recommendation originated from an incorrect item that was mistakenly added to the cart.

Although there was no indication of intentional misconduct, the agent's failure to validate the product details before making the recommendation resulted in a process deviation that could impact the integrity of the recommendation flow.
Recognition2:
Coaching Provided

I discussed the observation with the agent and explained the difference between proper recommendation practices and behaviors that may be classified as gaming or manipulation. I emphasized the importance of:

Carefully reading and verifying every product description before adding an item to the customer's cart.
Ensuring that any comparison or recommendation is based solely on the customer's intended item and not on an incorrectly selected product.
Avoiding actions that could unintentionally influence customer decisions through inaccurate product comparisons.
Taking time to validate item details before proceeding with recommendations to maintain compliance with company policies and provide an accurate customer experience.

I also recognized the agent for demonstrating integrity by immediately escalating the concern to Team Leader Gerald after realizing that she might have made an error. This willingness to seek guidance reflects accountability and a commitment to doing the right thing.
Recognition3:
Additional Coaching Reminder

I reminded the agent that while this incident appears to have been an unintentional process error and she demonstrated accountability by immediately escalating the concern, it is still considered a compliance issue. I clearly communicated that she is expected to apply the coaching provided and strictly follow the proper recommendation process on every call.

I further emphasized that any recurrence of the same behavior, whether intentional or unintentional, may result in the issuance of a Corrective Action (CA) in accordance with company policies and procedures. The agent acknowledged the expectation, understood the potential consequence of repeated violations, and committed to exercising greater diligence when verifying product details and providing recommendations to customers.

The agent has an opportunity to improve her attention to detail during the recommendation process by thoroughly verifying the product description, specifications, and item number before adding any item to the customer's cart. Every recommendation should be based solely on the customer's intended product to ensure accurate comparisons and maintain the integrity of the recommendation process.

Moving forward, the agent should slow down when navigating between product pages, carefully review the CTW, item description, and other relevant details before presenting alternatives, and avoid making recommendations based on an incorrectly selected item. Consistently applying these practices will help prevent unintentional manipulation, ensure compliance with company policies, and deliver a transparent and accurate customer experience.

AreaOfOpportunity:
Team Discussion Summary

During today's team discussion, we reminded everyone of the Zero Tolerance Policy (ZTP) scenarios that could result in immediate disciplinary action, including termination.

We emphasized that agents must never process customer payments under any circumstance, as payment processing is outside the scope of our support.

We also discussed the proper handling of disconnected calls. If a customer becomes unresponsive, agents should follow the appropriate ghost spiel, informing the customer that no response is being heard, advising that the call will be disconnected, and ensuring complete notes are documented on the account. In situations where a system issue causes the call to disconnect, agents are required to call the customer back immediately and document the incident thoroughly in the account notes.

Additionally, if an agent experiences a system issue close to the end of their shift, they are still expected to return to their workstation once the issue is resolved to properly log off all systems and complete the required end-of-shift procedures.

The team was reminded that all calls are recorded. Whenever a call is disconnected by an agent, an automated notification is sent to the leadership team for review. Each incident will be investigated, and if it is determined that the call was intentionally disconnected without following the proper process, it will be treated as a Zero Tolerance Policy (ZTP) violation.

We also reminded everyone that today remains a critical working day, and all agents are expected to report for their scheduled shifts unless otherwise approved.

The team was encouraged to consistently utilize all available support tools, follow the documented processes, and adhere to standard operating procedures to ensure quality customer service and compliance.

The team was also reminded to utilize the System Issue Tracker whenever they encounter any technical or system-related problems. All incidents must be documented immediately to ensure proper tracking, escalation, and resolution.

In addition, agents were instructed to maintain accurate documentation on every interaction. They must take detailed notes during each call, copy and paste any relevant pop-up system messages into the internal notes, and ensure that all customer interactions—particularly Dispatch and Blended calls—have complete, accurate, and timely account documentation before ending the interaction.

An update was also shared regarding the team's graduation ceremony. While the graduation has been confirmed, the official date has not yet been provided. The team will be informed as soon as the schedule is finalized.

Lastly, we reiterated the expectation for agents to arrive at least 30 minutes before their scheduled shift to allow sufficient time to connect to GlobalProtect and launch all required systems. Agents are compensated based on their scheduled phone time, provided they are ready to take calls on time. We also reminded the team that support personnel will wait only 20 minutes prior to the scheduled shift for agents to arrive. If an agent is not on-site within that timeframe, the available support staff will assume the workstation to ensure service coverage. As a result, the affected agent will be recorded as 30 minutes late, which will also impact their pay.

During today's team discussion, we reminded everyone of the Zero Tolerance Policy (ZTP) scenarios that could result in immediate disciplinary action, including termination.

We emphasized that agents must never process customer payments under any circumstance, as payment processing is outside the scope of our support.

We also discussed the proper handling of disconnected calls. If a customer becomes unresponsive, agents should follow the appropriate ghost spiel, informing the customer that no response is being heard, advising that the call will be disconnected, and ensuring complete notes are documented on the account. In situations where a system issue causes the call to disconnect, agents are required to call the customer back immediately and document the incident thoroughly in the account notes.

Additionally, if an agent experiences a system issue close to the end of their shift, they are still expected to return to their workstation once the issue is resolved to properly log off all systems and complete the required end-of-shift procedures.

The team was reminded that all calls are recorded. Whenever a call is disconnected by an agent, an automated notification is sent to the leadership team for review. Each incident will be investigated, and if it is determined that the call was intentionally disconnected without following the proper process, it will be treated as a Zero Tolerance Policy (ZTP) violation.

We also reminded everyone that today remains a critical working day, and all agents are expected to report for their scheduled shifts unless otherwise approved.

The team was encouraged to consistently utilize all available support tools, follow the documented processes, and adhere to standard operating procedures to ensure quality customer service and compliance.

The team was also reminded to utilize the System Issue Tracker whenever they encounter any technical or system-related problems. All incidents must be documented immediately to ensure proper tracking, escalation, and resolution.

In addition, agents were instructed to maintain accurate documentation on every interaction. They must take detailed notes during each call, copy and paste any relevant pop-up system messages into the internal notes, and ensure that all customer interactions—particularly Dispatch and Blended calls—have complete, accurate, and timely account documentation before ending the interaction.

An update was also shared regarding the team's graduation ceremony. While the graduation has been confirmed, the official date has not yet been provided. The team will be informed as soon as the schedule is finalized.

Lastly, we reiterated the expectation for agents to arrive at least 30 minutes before their scheduled shift to allow sufficient time to connect to GlobalProtect and launch all required systems. Agents are compensated based on their scheduled phone time, provided they are ready to take calls on time. We also reminded the team that support personnel will wait only 20 minutes prior to the scheduled shift for agents to arrive. If an agent is not on-site within that timeframe, the available support staff will assume the workstation to ensure service coverage. As a result, the affected agent will be recorded as 30 minutes late, which will also impact their pay.

In support of operational requirements, business continuity, and client service commitments, the following days are hereby designated as Critical Working Days. Employee attendance during these periods is essential to maintaining adequate staffing levels and ensuring uninterrupted operations.
Critical Working Days
The following are considered Critical Working Days:
A day before Payday
During Payday
A day after Payday
A day before a Holiday
During Holiday
A day after a Holiday
A day before a Scheduled Rest Day
A day after a Scheduled Rest Day
Attendance Expectations
All employees scheduled to work on Critical Working Days are expected to:
Report to work on time and complete their entire scheduled shift.
Maintain adherence to assigned schedules.
Avoid unauthorized absences, tardiness, undertime, and schedule deviations.
Submit leave requests in advance whenever possible and in accordance with company policies.
Immediately notify their Team Leader, Supervisor, or Manager in the event of emergencies or unforeseen circumstances that may affect attendance.
Compliance and Consequences
Attendance during Critical Working Days is closely monitored due to its significant impact on operational performance, workforce planning, and client commitments.
In accordance with the Company's Code of Conduct and Discipline (COCD):
Section 1.31 – Absence During a Critical Work Day
"Absence during a Critical Work Day such as a day before or after rest days, plotted vacation leaves, paydays, and holidays, whether on No Call No Show (NCNS) or an Unauthorized Absence (UA)."
Any employee who incurs an absence on a Critical Working Day, whether classified as a No Call No Show (NCNS) or an Unauthorized Absence (UA), shall be subject to the corresponding disciplinary action as prescribed under the Company's Code of Conduct and Discipline.
Employees are strongly encouraged to manage personal commitments responsibly and plan activities accordingly to avoid attendance issues during these critical periods. Failure to comply with attendance expectations may result in corrective and disciplinary action based on the nature and frequency of the offense.
Management reserves the right to review attendance records, investigate violations, and implement appropriate disciplinary measures consistent with company policies.
Your cooperation and commitment to maintaining operational excellence are highly appreciated.
Acknowledgement

In support of operational requirements, business continuity, and client service commitments, the following days are hereby designated as Critical Working Days. Employee attendance during these periods is essential to maintaining adequate staffing levels and ensuring uninterrupted operations.

A day after a Scheduled Rest Day
RootCause:
Attendance Expectations
All employees scheduled to work on Critical Working Days are expected to:
Report to work on time and complete their entire scheduled shift.
Maintain adherence to assigned schedules.
Avoid unauthorized absences, tardiness, undertime, and schedule deviations.
Submit leave requests in advance whenever possible and in accordance with company policies.
Immediately notify their Team Leader, Supervisor, or Manager in the event of emergencies or unforeseen circumstances that may affect attendance.
SmartGoal: Compliance and Consequences Attendance during Critical Working Days is closely monitored due to its significant impact on operational performance, workforce planning, and client commitments. In accordance with the Company's Code of Conduct and Discipline (COCD):
TaskName: Section 1.31 – Absence During a Critical Work Day "Absence during a Critical Work Day such as a day before or after rest days, plotted vacation leaves, paydays, and holidays, whether on No Call No Show (NCNS) or an Unauthorized Absence (UA)."
TaskDesc:
Any employee who incurs an absence on a Critical Working Day, whether classified as a No Call No Show (NCNS) or an Unauthorized Absence (UA), shall be subject to the corresponding disciplinary action as prescribed under the Company's Code of Conduct and Discipline.
Employees are strongly encouraged to manage personal commitments responsibly and plan activities accordingly to avoid attendance issues during these critical periods. Failure to comply with attendance expectations may result in corrective and disciplinary action based on the nature and frequency of the offense.
Management reserves the right to review attendance records, investigate violations, and implement appropriate disciplinary measures consistent with company policies.
Your cooperation and commitment to maintaining operational excellence are highly appreciated.

Critical Working Days and Attendance Compliance
In support of operational requirements, business continuity, and client service commitments, the following days are hereby designated as Critical Working Days. Employee attendance during these periods is essential to maintaining adequate staffing levels and ensuring uninterrupted operations.
BiggestRock:
Critical Working Days
The following are considered Critical Working Days:
A day before Payday
During Payday
A day after Payday
A day before a Holiday
During Holiday
A day after a Holiday
A day before a Scheduled Rest Day
A day after a Scheduled Rest Day
RootCause:
Attendance Expectations
All employees scheduled to work on Critical Working Days are expected to:
Report to work on time and complete their entire scheduled shift.
Maintain adherence to assigned schedules.
Avoid unauthorized absences, tardiness, undertime, and schedule deviations.
Submit leave requests in advance whenever possible and in accordance with company policies.
Immediately notify their Team Leader, Supervisor, or Manager in the event of emergencies or unforeseen circumstances that may affect attendance.
SmartGoal: Compliance and Consequences Attendance during Critical Working Days is closely monitored due to its significant impact on operational performance, workforce planning, and client commitments. In accordance with the Company's Code of Conduct and Discipline (COCD):
TaskName: Section 1.31 – Absence During a Critical Work Day "Absence during a Critical Work Day such as a day before or after rest days, plotted vacation leaves, paydays, and holidays, whether on No Call No Show (NCNS) or an Unauthorized Absence (UA)."
TaskDesc:
Any employee who incurs an absence on a Critical Working Day, whether classified as a No Call No Show (NCNS) or an Unauthorized Absence (UA), shall be subject to the corresponding disciplinary action as prescribed under the Company's Code of Conduct and Discipline.
Employees are strongly encouraged to manage personal commitments responsibly and plan activities accordingly to avoid attendance issues during these critical periods. Failure to comply with attendance expectations may result in corrective and disciplinary action based on the nature and frequency of the offense.
Management reserves the right to review attendance records, investigate violations, and implement appropriate disciplinary measures consistent with company policies.
Your cooperation and commitment to maintaining operational excellence are highly appreciated.

ACTION PLAN – OON DISPATCH NO REFERRAL PROCESS COMPLIANCE REINFORCEMENT
1. Start-of-Shift Compliance Gate & Tool Readiness by RSA Persona
All agents must ensure the correct tools and job aids are open and available before beginning servicing, based on call type:
A. Intake Calls (Customer-Initiated Roadside Assistance Requests)
Focus: Initial job creation, service determination, coverage review, customer verification
Required Tool:
Intake Call Flow Optimization & Call Control Tips Job Aid
B. Dispatch Calls (Service Provider Coordination & Updates)
Focus: Provider coordination, ETA updates, assignment handling, service progress monitoring
Required Tools:
Dispatch Call Flow Optimization & Call Control Tips Job Aid
Manual Dispatch Tool (Primary tool for all dispatch transactions and provider engagement)
C. Customer Solutions Calls (Escalations & Case Resolution)
Focus: Escalated cases, delayed services, incomplete resolutions, customer dissatisfaction, advanced troubleshooting
Required Tools:
Customer Solutions Call Flow Optimization Job Aid
SATT (Solutions and Troubleshooting Tool)
2. Daily Compliance Reminders (Huddle Reinforcement Points)
Always follow the correct call flow based on RSA persona (Intake, Dispatch, Solutions)
Always call the customer first on applicable OON dispatches
Always click the customer’s phone number directly from Swoop (copy-paste into Avaya is strictly prohibited)
Always offer Schedule Dispatch first when applicable
Continue contacting up to 8 Out-of-Network providers when required
Follow approved No Referral scripting verbatim
Utilize AVA for clarification when uncertain
3. Job Aid Utilization Requirement
Agents are expected to actively use the correct tools during live servicing:
Intake Call Flow Optimization & Call Control Tips – Intake interactions
Dispatch Call Flow Optimization & Call Control Tips – provider coordination and dispatch handling
Manual Dispatch Tool – dispatch execution and provider engagement
Customer Solutions Call Flow Optimization – escalations and resolutions
SATT Tool – case resolution and troubleshooting
AVA (Ask Agero Virtual Assistance) – process clarification support
4. Agent Acknowledgement & Compliance Confirmation
All agents are required to acknowledge understanding of:
No Referral Process compliance requirements
Proper tool usage per RSA persona
OON dispatch execution standards
Customer contact and scripting adherence
5. Immediate Coaching & Reinforcement
Any compliance gaps identified will be addressed through documented coaching sessions to reinforce expectations and ensure corrective action.

## ZERO TOLERANCE POLICY (ZTP) – NON-NEGOTIABLE

Any violation of the Zero Tolerance Policy is considered a terminable offense. No exceptions will be made.

### 1. Never Process Payments

Agents are strictly prohibited from processing credit card payments or any other form of payment.

### 2. Maintain Professional Conduct

All agents are expected to demonstrate professionalism, respect, and empathy during every customer interaction. Rude, disrespectful, or inappropriate behavior will not be tolerated.

### 3. No Call Avoidance

Agents must not engage in any form of call avoidance, including but not limited to:

* Unassigning jobs
* Leaving jobs idle without action
* Placing customers on excessive hold without progress
* Intentionally disconnecting calls
* Performing improper transfers
* Avoiding escalated calls
* Misusing hold or snooze functions

## Operational Standards

All agents are expected to adhere to the following operational requirements:

* Answer all incoming calls within five (5) seconds.
* Complete required system actions within five (5) seconds, including:

  * Call Customer
  * Create Job
  * Edit Draft
* Follow established processes and utilize all available tools and resources.
* Avoid unnecessary long calls and extended hold times.
* Document all actions accurately in Job Details and Internal Notes.

### Callback Notification – Agent Assigned to Job

Agents assigned to a job must call the assigned dispatcher's extension to determine ownership of the job. If the dispatcher does not answer, the agent must immediately assign the job to themselves and take full ownership.

## Golden Rule

* Own the call.
* Follow the process.
* Document everything.
* Zero exceptions.

**Remember: If you touch the job, you own the job.**

Recognition1:
My coaching session with Rod today focused on a customer scenario that Brandon brought to my attention regarding tire age and the applicable refund options. The customer received a tire that was believed to be more than four years old. Based on our policy, if a customer receives a tire that is past the four-year mark, they may either return the tire for a full refund or keep the tire and receive a 50% refund.

During the interaction, Rod initially offered the 50% refund, which was the correct process. However, he later contacted the customer and advised that no refund could be provided because he believed the tire was still within the four-year guideline. During our coaching discussion, I asked Rod where the confusion came from. He explained that he was unsure how to interpret the SOP regarding tires that are past the four-year mark and was uncertain whether a tire that exceeded four years by only a short period would still qualify.

Rod also shared that he sought assistance from Chaz regarding the tire's DOT, which indicated a manufacturing date in 2022. During the discussion, there was confusion around determining whether the tire was still within the four-year guideline based solely on the year. Together, we reviewed the SOP and clarified that determining tire age requires reviewing not only the year but also the specific week and month of manufacture. This ensures an accurate calculation of whether the tire is still within or has exceeded the four-year guideline.

In this instance, confusion around determining whether a tire was within or beyond the four-year guideline led to inconsistent information being provided to the customer. Strengthening policy validation and clarification before providing a final answer will help ensure accuracy and consistency in customer resolutions.
RootCause: This behavior is happening due to a misunderstanding of the SOP and how the four-year tire age guideline should be calculated. This knowledge gap led to uncertainty when applying the policy and resulted in inconsistent communication to the customer.

Melvon did not clearly emphasize the submission deadline or fiscal year policy, which the member found misleading. Admin has made an exception for part of the claims so the funds were partially salvaged.

Melvon has also replied unprofessionally with unacceptable spelling mistakes - this needs to be taken seriously as a small typo every once in a while is understandable, but to have 5 mistakes in 2 sentences is absolutely atrocious.
BiggestRock:
We’re all familiar with how the Gusto card functions, but in this case, I followed the usual “wrong wallet” adjustment approach that we use for other policies. I confirmed that the expense could be considered eligible under those wallets, so I proceeded with the adjustment.
However, I completely overlooked the 5-merchant restriction specific to the Gusto AI stipend wallet. Because of that, I processed the transactions when I shouldn’t have.
This was mainly due to my lack of full familiarity with Gusto AI-specific rules, combined with rushing through tickets at the time. I recognize that I missed an important policy detail, and that’s on me. The issue came down to me moving too quickly and making assumptions I shouldn’t have. I focused on helping the member submit their reimbursement right away, but I didn’t take a step back to clearly explain the key policy details—especially the April 30 deadline and the fact that unused funds don’t roll over. I assumed the member already knew this, and because of that, I failed to properly call it out, which led to confusion. I meant to clarify that the member can resubmit expensed within eligible period.
 
The writing errors were also on me. I rushed my response and didn’t take the time to proofread before sending it. That’s not my usual standard, but in this case, I missed it, and I understand how that came across as unprofessional.
RootCause:
The primary behavioral root cause was rushing through ticket handling, which led to assumptions being made instead of fully validating policy details. While the agent was familiar with the general Gusto card and “wrong wallet” adjustment process, there was a failure to pause and confirm the AI Wallet’s specific restriction to five approved merchants. This resulted in applying a standard process that did not apply to the Gusto AI stipend wallet.
Another contributing factor was incomplete policy awareness, particularly regarding Gusto AI–specific rules, including the five‑merchant limitation, the April 30 expense deadline, and the non‑rollover of unused funds. The agent assumed the member already understood these policies and, as a result, did not clearly explain them. This assumption created confusion for the member and led to incorrect expectations.
Additionally, there was an overemphasis on resolving the member’s concern quickly rather than ensuring accuracy and policy compliance. The intent to be helpful outweighed the need to slow down, validate eligibility, and clearly set boundaries based on policy.
Finally, lack of attention to communication quality was observed. Rushing resulted in writing errors and missed proofreading, which does not align with expected professionalism and further reduced clarity in the interaction.
Overall, the root cause was a combination of speed over accuracy, assumptions over validation, and insufficient policy reinforcement, rather than a lack of intent or effort.

Recognition1:
Coaching Discussion: KASOCIUS Timekeeping Scrubbing
Wave: 32
Facilitator:Janille/Flora mae
Date:April 16
Recognition2:
Payroll Cut-Off Reminder:
Agents were informed of the payroll cut-off schedule:
15th of the month → Salary released on the 25th
30th of the month → Salary released on the 10th
Given these timelines, agents are expected to complete all scrubbing and correction submissions before the cut-off dates to ensure accurate payroll processing.
Recognition3:
Payslip Viewing Expectations:
Initial payslip viewing becomes available after the cut-off date.
Final payslip will be available 3 days before the salary release date.
Agents were reminded that any uncorrected discrepancies beyond the cut-off may no longer be reflected in the upcoming payroll cycle.
AreaOfOpportunity:
Objective:
To ensure all agents properly manage and scrub their KASOCIUS timekeeping on a daily basis, minimizing payroll discrepancies and ensuring accurate salary processing.
Actual: Daily time in and out and correction submission
BiggestRock:
iscussion Points:
The team was aligned on the importance of daily KASOCIUS timekeeping maintenance (scrubbing). Agents were reminded that submitting corrections should not be delayed and must be done on a daily basis to avoid accumulation of errors.
RootCause:
It was emphasized that all agents must:
Log in and log out properly in KASOCIUS to ensure accurate tracking of working hours.
Submit KASOCIUS correction requests daily for any discrepancies observed in their attendance.
Regularly check their KASOCIUS calendar, paying attention to color coding which indicates attendance status.
Review and validate their Clock-In (CC In) and Clock-Out (CC Out) entries to ensure correctness.
SmartGoal: mportant Guidance on Correction Requests: The team was specifically advised that when submitting correction requests: The Time In and Time Out fields (upper boxes) must not be left blank. These entries should always be aligned with their correct scheduled shift on the specific date. It was further explained that accuracy in these fields is critical, as incomplete or incorrect entries may result in payroll discrepancies.
TaskDesc:
Reason for Daily Corrections:
The team was provided clarity on why correction requests are necessary, even if they have already manually updated their time:
The system may default the Time In and Time Out to 10:00 PM – 6:00 AM, regardless of the agent’s actual schedule.
Because of this default setting, agents are still required to submit correction requests to properly tag their actual working hours.
Even if agents have manually encoded their schedules in KASOCIUS, daily validation and correction submission is still required to ensure accuracy.
EmployeeCommitment:
This process ensures that:
Their actual schedule is correctly reflected, and
Any mismatch caused by default system settings is properly corrected before payroll processing.
LeaderCommitment:
Expectation Setting:
The team was clearly advised that ownership of timekeeping accuracy lies with each individual agent. Daily compliance is critical to avoid payroll issues and delays.
FollowUpPlan:
Action Items:
Perform daily KASOCIUS scrubbing and submit corrections immediately.
Ensure Time In and Time Out fields are properly filled and aligned with schedule.
Practice accurate login/logout behavior moving forward.
Monitor attendance calendar daily for discrepancies.
Coordinate with Team Leads for any concerns regarding corrections or OT plotting.
